title: Transplantation of UC-MSCs on a collagen scaffold restores ovarian function in mice with POF
author: Yanjun Yang

steps_raw.instruction: UC-MSC isolation and culture.

Human umbilical cord tissues were collected from after normal vaginal delivery of full-term births at the Delivery Room of the Affiliated Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School and processed within 12 h of natural delivery. UC-MSCs were isolated according to published methods [21]. After vessels were mechanically removed, the umbilical cord was manually dissected into small sections. The segment tissues were cultured in complete growth medium consisting of low-glucose Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (LG-DMEM; GIBCO, Grand Island, NY, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS; Hyclone, Logan, UT, USA), 100 U/mL penicillin (GIBCO), and 100 mg/mL streptomycin (GIBCO). The first colony of UC-MSCs was observed after approximately 14 days. Human UC-MSCs at passages 3-5 were used for the following experiments.
Flow cytometry analysis.

Flow cytometry was used to analyze UC-MSCs surface marker expression at passage 3. The cells were incubated for 1 h with fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)- or phycoreythrin (PE)-conjugated antibodies against human CD13 (eBioscience, Colorado, USA), CD29 (eBioscience), CD34 (BD Pharmingen, San Diego, CA, USA), CD45 (eBioscience), CD73 (BD Pharmingen), CD90 (eBioscience), CD105 (eBioscience), CD146 (BD Pharmingen), and HLA-DR (eBioscience).
Differentiation of UC-MSCs.

At passage 3, the cells were assessed for multipotency using adipogenic, osteogenic and neural-like differentiation assays. Briefly, cells were cultured in adipogenic induction medium (GIBCO) for 14 days. Oil red O staining (Sigma, Steinheim, Germany) was used as an indicator of intracellular lipid accumulation. Osteogenesis was induced by osteogenic induction medium (GIBCO) for 28 days and calcium deposition was observed via alizarin red staining (Sigma). Cells were treated with the pre-induction medium containing 10-7 M all-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA; Sigma) and 10 ng/ml bFGF (GIBCO) for 24 h, and then treated with modified MNM medium for 36 h for neural-like differentiation. The expression of neuron-speciﬁc enolase (1:100, sc-292097, Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Santa Cruz, CA, USA) and neuroﬁlament medium polypeptide (1:100, sc-16143, Santa Cruz Biotechnology) in induced UC-MSCs was detected by immunoﬂuorescence staining.
Preparation of collagen/UC-MSCs.

Scaffolds (collagen type I) were obtained from the State Key Laboratory of Molecular Developmental Biology (GMP grade, Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China) and were prepared as previously described [20]. Collagen (20 mg) was dissolved in 2 mL PBS and pipetted repeatedly to form gelatinous scaffolds. The final concentration of degradable collagen mixed with UC-MSCs was 5 mg/ml. The collagen/UC-MSCs were produced from UC-MSCs seeded on a collagen scaffold (collagen/UC-MSCs) in 24-well plates. The transplant components were put on ice and mixed immediately prior to injection.
Preparation of the premature ovarian failure mouse model.

Adult female C57BL/6 mice (6 weeks of age) were purchased from the Model Animal Research Center of Nanjing University and housed in IVC cages at the Drum Tower Hospital Animal Experimental Center. Mice were maintained under controlled lighting (lights on 0700–1900 h) and temperature (22℃), with ad libitum access to food and water. Vaginal smears were obtained daily and only mice showing 2 consecutive normal 4-day estrus cycles were used in experiments.

Adult female C57BL/6 mice were treated with CTX (H32020857, Jiangsu Shengdi Pharmaceutical Industry Co. Limited, Jiangsu, China) at 40 mg/kg/day intraperitoneally for 15 days. An equal volume of sterile water was given to mice in the control group.

2.6. Transplantation of collagen/UC-MSCs. Mice with POF were randomly divided into four groups according to different treatments as follows: PBS group, collagen group, UC-MSC group and collagen/UC-MSC group. The control group consisted of normal mice, which received no treatment. Mice were anesthetized with chloral hydrate (4 ml/kg) and then ﬁxed in a decubitus position and shaved. The ovaries were exposed through a micro-incision on the back. Aliquot suspensions (10μl) were injected into the core of the ovaries in a retrograde manner, through the maximum ovary cross-section using 0.33-mm (29G) needles on BD Ultra-FineTM 1.0-ml disposable insulin syringes (Becton Dickinson and Company, Franklin Lakes, NJ, USA). For the PBS group, 10μl PBS was injected per ovary. For the collagen group, 10μl of degradable collagen was injected per ovary. For the UC-MSC group, 2×105 UC-MSCs in 10μl PBS was injected. In the collagen/UC-MSC group, 2×105 UC-MSCs in 10μl degradable collagen was injected. Two weeks after injection, vaginal smears were obtained daily for 2 consecutive estrus cycles.
Mice hormone detection.

Four weeks after transplantation, the mice were anesthetized with chloral hydrate during diestrus and blood was collected from the posterior orbital venous plexus. The blood sample was then centrifuged and the plasma was frozen at -80℃ for hormone analysis. The concentrations of plasma follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and E2 were measured using the ELISA kit (YANYU, Shanghai, China); the AMH was measured using a different ELISA kit (CEA228Mu, Cloud-Clone Corp, Wuhan, China).
Ovarian morphology and follicle counting.

After blood was collected, the ovaries were removed and ﬁxed in Bouin’s solution. After ﬁxation for 4-6 h, the samples were dehydrated and embedded in parafﬁn. A conventional method was used including the trimming of the ovarian area, slicing into 5 μm thick sections and every fifth section was staining with hematoxylin and eosin (HE). Follicle counting was performed using an unbiased stereological method. Only follicles with an oocyte nucleus were counted. The total number of follicles was then multiplied by ﬁve. Follicles were classiﬁed according to the classiﬁcation of a previous investigation [22].
Immunohistochemistry (IHC).

Ovaries were fixed in 10% buffered-formalin for 12 h. After embedded and sectioned at 5 μm, samples were deparaffinized, rehydrated, and endogenous peroxidase activity was blocked by incubation in Reagent A/B (Sangon, China) for 10 min. Tissue samples were immunolabeled with anti-Ki67 antibody (Ki67, 1:400, ab16667, Abcam, Cambridge, UK) and anti-Cleaved-Caspase3 antibody (Cleaved-Caspase3, 1:300, 9661, Cell Signaling Technology, Beverly, MA, USA) overnight at 4 ℃. The sections were then washed 3 times in PBS, incubated with goat anti rabbit secondary antibody and stained with DAB reagent (Zhongshan Jinqiao Biotechnology Co, Ltd, Beijing, China). Primary antibodies were replaced with non-immune rabbit IgG in some sections to serve as the negative control.
Statistical analysis.

Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS 19.0 (Version 22.0, IBM Corp, Armonk, NY, USA). The means ± SD of the data were calculated. Either the Student’s t-test or t’-test was used to determine significance between the two groups and multiple comparisons were done via one-way analysis of variance. A P value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
